answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks using distributed radio-path tomography. A node proves presence by broadcasting pulses whose propagation delays are measured across receivers stationed near an alpine glacier, an open knoll, and a juniper grove. Fabricating identities requires an attacker to deploy discrete transceivers across these sites, incurring steep hardware and land-access costs. However, shifting atmospheric humidity alters signal transit times, causing false rejections.
